messages:
incident-bot: Page triggered — severity: high. Noted sustained p95 latency increase for text generation in eu-west-1 (dedicated pool). Autoscaling and routing policies applied; paging on-call.

elena: Acknowledged, joining. KV-cache eviction rate jumped at ~14:03 UTC, plus higher disk read waits.

sanjay: Corroborating metrics: eviction spike + working set churn after yesterday's runtime prefetch change. Putting logs into thread.

mike: I'm rolling back the prefetch tweak I deployed at 13:50. Initiating canary rollback for eu-west-1 now.

ops-bot: Autoscaler: launching +4 instances in eu-west-1 (pool:d-ed-2). Expected ready ~2m.

julia: Draft status page note ready for review: "Investigating increased inference response times in eu-west-1. Engineers are mitigating and traffic may be routed to other regions temporarily. No data loss expected. Next update in 15 minutes." Thoughts?

samir: Working a hotfix to reduce eviction pressure: increase in-memory TTL and disable prefetch for long-sequence requests >1024 tokens. Preparing deploy.

sanjay: Paste: logs from edge node (snippet):
```
2026-03-17T13:59:12Z [kv] eviction: keys=1.21M target=800k rate=1250/sec
2026-03-17T13:59:13Z [runtime] prefetch: queued=460 latency_ms=1700
2026-03-17T13:59:14Z [serving] p95=2180ms p50=330ms
```

elena: That matches the pattern we saw in staging. If scaling and routing hold we can avoid customer-impacting fallbacks.

mike: Rollback complete on canary. Draining canary tasks and shifting traffic back to stable.

ops-bot: Routing adjusted: shift 25% EU traffic -> us-central-1, 10% -> ap-south-1. Rules applied.

julia: Customer advisory (short list) draft: "We are investigating higher-than-normal response times for inference in eu-west-1. We have applied routing and scaling mitigations and expect recovery within 30–45 minutes. We will post an update once normal latencies resume. Apologies for the disruption."

support-bot: Template note: include status page link + recommended retry/backoff guidance and avoid sending very large context sequences for 30m.

samir: Hotfix deployed to eu-west-1 workers: TTL increased, prefetch disabled for seqs >1024, observability flags enabled for eviction debugging.

sanjay: Post-hotfix metrics: p95 reduced from ~2180ms -> ~790ms over ~90s, eviction rate down to ~380/sec.

elena: Good improvement. Monitor for any rise in error rates or token truncations.

mike: No 5xx spike observed. Token generation continues without timeouts. Baseline p95 still elevated but trending down.

julia: Posting initial status page update now.

incident-bot: Status page update published: https://status.redwood-inference.example/incident/2026-03-17-eu-kv-evictions

elena: I'll hand off to daytime on-call @sanjay in ~25m. I'll remain until p95 < 500ms for 10m straight or until handoff.

sanjay: Acknowledged. I'll continue follow-ups: increase pool target if necessary, validate routing, and keep customer comms updated.

support-bot: Sending templated advisory to affected workspace owners (n=12) — includes retry/backoff guidance and status link.

mike: Watching memory after TTL bump — no OOMs so far.

samir: Action items: 1) Revisit prefetch heuristic for long sequences, 2) Add eviction alert threshold at 800/sec, 3) Add a canary test for large-context workloads.

elena: Keep messages concise in this thread. I'll update again for the handoff summary.

sanjay: Latest: p95=455ms p50=300ms eviction_rate=305/sec. Routing stable. Ready to take handoff in 5.

elena: Handoff: leaving the bridge. Oncall: @sanjay. Summary: Pre-fetch tweak caused KV eviction surge → p95 spike. Mitigations: rolled back prefetch change, deployed hotfix (TTL + disable prefetch for large sequences), scaled pool, partial traffic reroute. Customer notice posted. Current state: recovering. ETA to normal: 15–25 minutes if eviction rate remains low.

sanjay: Taking over. Will post next update in 10 minutes or sooner if anything changes.

incident-bot: Incident status: monitoring. Severity downgraded to medium.
